bib.title: Multitask Prompted Training Enables Zero-Shot Task Generalization

read.skipped: Appendix G prompt listing (about 170k chars of templates) skimmed only via its contents page; references skimmed.

question: Can zero-shot generalization to held-out tasks be induced directly by explicit multitask training on many datasets rewritten as natural-language prompts?
hypothesis: Implicit multitask supervision in pretraining plays a large role in zero-shot generalization, so explicit supervised multitask prompted training should induce it without massive scale and make the model more robust to prompt wording.
contributions: A templating language and tool (PromptSource) for mapping datasets to prompts, and the Public Pool of Prompts (P3) with 2073 prompts for 177 datasets
T0, T0+ and T0++: T5+LM 11B fine-tuned on a multitask prompted mixture, with strong zero-shot results on held-out tasks and BIG-bench
Ablations on prompts per dataset and number of datasets, and a prompt-robustness comparison with GPT-3
Release of models, prompts and materialized data

method.summary: Fine-tune LM-adapted T5 (3B and 11B) with maximum likelihood on a shuffled mixture of 39 (T0), 49 (T0+) or 55 (T0++) datasets, each rendered through many prompt templates. Evaluate zero-shot on whole held-out tasks (NLI, coreference, sentence completion, WSD) and 14 BIG-bench tasks, reporting median and interquartile range across prompts.

models.name: T0
models.init_from: T5+LM 11B (Lester et al. 2021: T5 plus 100B more tokens of LM objective on C4)

other.T5 pretraining: masked LM on 1T tokens of C4

other.mixture: adds SuperGLUE except RTE and CB

other.davinci: used via OpenAI API for RTE robustness check, assumed 175B (Gao et al. 2021)

training.objective: standard maximum likelihood, autoregressive generation of target given input
training.batch_size: 1024 sequences (2^20 total input tokens per batch)
training.tokens: about 250 billion tokens across all training runs incl. preliminary experiments
training.compute: about 270 total hours on v3-512 for all runs; about 27 h per single T0 run; about 8.9 tCO2e

other.checkpoint selection: highest score on validation splits of training datasets
other.ablations: same hyperparameters and same number of steps across p ablations

inference.decoding: rank classification: pick the answer option with highest log-likelihood under the model, no length normalization
inference.samples: all P3 prompts per dataset (about 10 per held-out dataset); median and IQR reported; single run
inference.prompting: zero-shot, no examples; prompts from P3; BIG-bench prompts from maintainers

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction correct under rank classification; median over prompts, interquartile range Q3-Q1 as robustness

eval.protocol: Validation splits, true zero-shot (no held-out example used to select checkpoint or prompt); median and IQR over prompts; no seeds or significance tests.

limits: Zero-shot performance still lags models fine-tuned per task (Appendix B.2).
Task taxonomy is a heuristic; held-out tasks may overlap with training QA data (D.2).
Authors remain agnostic about why prompts support generalization (Section 2).
More datasets does not consistently reduce prompt-wording variance (Section 6.2).
Differences from FLAN (architecture, prompt diversity) are hypotheses left to future work (Section 7).
Contamination: HellaSwag 9.12% and RTE hypotheses 5.2% overlap with C4 (Appendix E).
T0++ gives biased or conspiracist answers (Table 2); not bias free.
Checkpoint steps, learning-rate schedule, warmup and seeds are not stated; single training run, no significance tests.
